raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

On SM100, the sparse indexer's prefill builds DeepGEMM's per-SM `mqa_logits` schedule once per prefill chunk and passes it to `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits` in every indexer layer that scores the chunk. Without a schedule, DeepGEMM runs its unbalanced kernel variant, which is slow when rows' KV ranges differ a lot, as in prefix-cache hits on long contexts. The MX weight cast also runs once per layer instead of once per chunk.

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill on a 128K-token prefix-cache hit: the dense indexer logits are 17–26% faster (GB200).
- Whole-model forward (`vllm bench forward`, real weights, DSpark, DEP2 on GB300) over 52 prefill shapes: 0.8% faster on average at 128K–160K cached tokens (up to 1.2%), 0.3–0.4% at 64K–96K, unchanged (within ±0.1%) for cold prefills and short prefix hits.
- Logits are bit-identical; GSM8K, passkey and DSpark acceptance unchanged.

## Validation

Indexer logits of one forward (the 4 dense indexer layers of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with `indexer_sparse_logits`, MXFP4 Q/K, one request of cached + new tokens), one GB200, torch profiler kernel sums, median of 3 runs:

| cached + new | main (ms) | This PR (ms) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 + 8K | 0.27 | 0.27 | 0 |
| 0 + 32K | 3.10 | 3.02 | -2.5% |
| 64K + 16K | 7.21 | 6.30 | -12.6% |
| 128K + 1K | 0.99 | 0.73 | -25.8% |
| 128K + 8K | 7.20 | 5.71 | -20.7% |
| 128K + 32K | 31.44 | 26.23 | -16.6% |

`vllm bench forward`, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with dummy weights, DEP2 on one GB200 node, FlashMLA MegaAttn with the MXFP4 indexer and `deep_select` top-k, `--kv-len-jitter 0 --max-num-batched-tokens 20480`, rank 0 kernel profile (`--profile-dir`) of `--case hit8k=8192@139264` (128K cached + 8K new):

| | main (us) | This PR (us) |
|---|---|---|
| `sm100_mqa_logits` | 4619 | 3601 |
| `sm100_mqa_logits_metadata` (new) | 0 | 27 |
| forward GPU span | 107631 | 106589 |

Whole-model forward, `vllm bench forward` on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with real weights and fixed real prompt tokens, DSpark K=5 (target + drafter timed), DEP2 on one GB300 node, same backends as above, FlashInfer autotune off, `--routing real --samples 5 --iters 10 --kv-len-jitter 0 --max-num-batched-tokens 20480`. CUDA-graph event time, max over DP ranks. Both arms ran on `fac2ce2eb3` (this PR applied on top), interleaved across the node's two GPU pairs (pair 0: main → PR, pair 1: PR → main), so each number is the mean of one run per pair. Per-case sample spread was ≤0.6%.

| 8K cached | 5 | +0.01% | -0.07% to +0.06% |

| batched / mixed | 12 | -0.53% | -1.19% to +0.08% |

| GSM8K, lm_eval 5-shot, max 1024 tokens, concurrency 32, strict-match | | 0.931 |
| DSpark acceptance length over the GSM8K run | | 3.447 |

Tests on GB200, and again on GB300 after the last commit:

```
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_tp_row_shard.py tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py
184 passed
```

`test_deepgemm_fp8_mqa_logits` now also checks that the scheduled kernel returns the same logits bit for bit.

## Details

- `get_mqa_logits_metadata()` wraps DeepGEMM's schedule builder and returns None off SM100 or where the installed DeepGEMM lacks it; `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits()` passes an optional `schedule_meta` through.

It is keyed by the row window, so TP row-sharded ranks share theirs too, and by capture state, so a captured graph never reads a schedule built eagerly.
- Decode already passes `schedule_metadata` to the paged kernel; this does the same for prefill.
- Not a duplicate: no open PR passes a schedule to the prefill logits; #63038 changes how prefill chunks are budgeted, which this does not touch.
